mission: Second survey world, same markings cut by the same hand into different stone. Desh overlays the two sites on the nav chart and draws the line. The bearing points into uncharted space.
why_now: One site is curiosity; two is a pattern the survey route can no longer absorb. Ben either folds the second world into the official report or he follows the line Desh has just drawn.
conflict: The survey route Luke designed runs exactly along the wrongness's bearing — coincidence or design. Ben does not know if Luke planned this, and he does not want to know yet.
turning_point: Desh lays the two anomalous sites on the nav chart and extends the line into a chart-sector that does not officially exist. Ben punches the coordinates and the empty sector stares back.
opening_hook: The second world has the same markings. Different climate, different geology, same hand.
closing_hook: The bearing points to a cluster of systems that do not appear on any navigation chart Ben has ever seen. Something is out there.
emotional_trajectory: Confirmation dread -> analytical focus -> determined pursuit

stakes.personal: Ben's growing certainty that this is bigger than a survey mission
stakes.interpersonal: Desh reads Ben's tension; the friendship holds while the scope outgrows the job
stakes.external: The pattern points toward something deliberately hidden from modern records

setting: Second survey world — different biome, same era of ruins — then back aboard the Steady Returns for analysis
sensory_details: The wrongness stronger here — Force-perception arriving at a slight parallax to the body, distances feeling fractionally unreliable; local vegetation patterns seasonally out of phase; Desh's navigation console showing the bearing line cutting through empty chart-space; the second world's ruins carry the same vibration in ancient stone that has no physical source

notes: Thin-place effects slightly stronger than at the first world. Desh might notice temperature inconsistencies or sound carrying oddly — non-Force-sensitive baseline establishing. Pacing: this is the fastest scene in Act 1 — confirm and move. Keep it tight. The pattern is already established from the previous scene; this scene confirms that it is deliberate. Diagnostic-voice trap — Ben should not, in this scene, articulate the pattern as a settled claim about who built it or why. He recognises the hand and punches the coordinates. Interpretation belongs to Ch3 when the perimeter facility does the explaining.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben crouches to examine identical markings carved into different-composition stone on a different world, confirming the hand that made them.
key_beats.state_change: The abstract wrongness from the first site becomes concrete repetition — the pattern is not local anomaly but deliberate placement.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Confirmation dread arrives as a physical sensation — a tightness in the chest, the instinct to move rather than sit with the implication. Ben's body wants action before his mind has finished processing what the repetition means.

key_beats.beat_description: Desh overlays the two anomalous sites on the nav chart and draws a line through uncharted space, extending the bearing into chart-sectors that do not officially exist.
key_beats.state_change: The scene pivots from archaeological confirmation to navigational crisis — the pattern now has a direction, and that direction points toward something deliberately hidden from modern records.
key_beats.pov_reaction: The pressure shifts from dread to analytical focus. Ben's attention narrows onto the line Desh has drawn, the coordinates, the empty space beyond. He reads Desh's tension in the set of his shoulders, recognizes the moment his friend understands the scope has outgrown the job, and chooses not to voice it yet.

key_beats.beat_description: Ben punches the bearing coordinates into the nav computer and stares at the empty chart sector beyond, waiting for the system to resolve or confirm the void.
key_beats.state_change: The bearing locks in. The next-scene pressure crystallizes at the boundary: something is out there, and Ben now carries the knowledge that Luke's survey route runs exactly along the wrongness's bearing — coincidence or design, Ben does not know yet and does not want to know yet.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Determined pursuit settles into Ben's posture. The dread has resolved into forward momentum. He is braced for the handoff, ready to follow the line or defend the choice not to, but no longer able to treat this as a routine survey.
